question: What is the primary focus of modern occupational health nursing?
explanation: Occupational health nursing centers on safeguarding the health, safety, and overall well-being of employees across various work environments. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h1)

question: How has the role of the workplace nurse changed over time?

options.A: It narrowed down to only treating minor cuts and dispensing simple pain relievers.
options.B: It shifted from basic first-aid treatment to comprehensive health promotion and hazard analysis.
options.C: It moved away from factory settings to focus exclusively on community pediatric care.
options.D: It stopped working with management and now only answers to labor unions.

explanation: Great job thinking about how nursing grows! While early industrial nurses mostly handled simple cuts and bruises, today's occupational health nurses focus on broad prevention, ergonomics, and keeping workers safe every day.

question: What is the core belief behind occupational health?

options.A: Workers should accept all workplace risks as part of the job.
options.B: Medical treatment is more important than hazard prevention.
options.C: Company profits must always outweigh employee health concerns.
options.D: Work should never cause injury, illness, or harm to the worker.

explanation: Spot on! The golden rule of occupational health is simple: no one should ever go to work and come back sick or injured. Safety always comes first.

question: Why is medical confidentiality especially critical in occupational health nursing?

options.A: To prevent employers from using private health data to unfairly penalize workers
options.B: To hide mistakes made by the occupational health clinic staff
options.C: To comply with tax laws regarding employee salaries and benefits
options.D: To stop other workers from knowing about common workplace injuries

explanation: Nurses must protect medical information so employees can seek care freely without fear of losing their jobs or facing discrimination. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h2)

question: Which Nigerian law sets the main minimum standards for factory safety and worker welfare?
explanation: You'll see this often in Nigerian public health! The Factories Act is the key law that protects workers and regulates safety conditions in Nigerian workplaces.

question: A factory worker in Lagos is injured by a machine. Which Nigerian agency and act handle employee compensation?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Education under the Scholarship Board Act
options.B: Central Bank of Nigeria under the Banking and Financial Services Act
options.C: Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund under the Employees' Compensation Act
options.D: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control under the Food Act

explanation: Don't let the long options trick you! The Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF) runs the Employees' Compensation Act to make sure injured workers get supported.

question: Which category of workplace hazard includes exposure to loud machinery noise and extreme heat?
explanation: Noise, vibration, radiation, and extreme temperatures are classified as physical workplace hazards. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a workplace risk assessment?

options.A: To evaluate how likely a hazard is to cause harm and determine appropriate controls
options.B: To replace all human workers with automated robotic machinery
options.C: To calculate the exact financial profit generated by each department
options.D: To find reasons to terminate employees who report minor injuries

explanation: Think of a risk assessment as looking ahead: we spot the danger, see how likely it is to hurt someone, and put rules in place to stop accidents before they happen.

question: What is the main goal of routine health check-ups in the workplace?

options.A: To determine the exact monthly salary of each employee
options.B: To help the company fire workers who take sick leave
options.C: To diagnose unrelated personal illnesses like childhood malaria
options.D: To detect early signs of work-related illness before permanent damage occurs

explanation: Early detection is key in nursing! Routine checks catch small health issues early on, stopping them from turning into major, long-term illnesses.

question: Why would an occupational health nurse test the hearing of workers in a noisy textile mill?

options.A: To identify early signs of noise-induced hearing loss before it worsens
options.B: To check if employees are listening to unauthorized radio stations
options.C: To measure how fast the machinery is producing textile materials
options.D: To test the general intelligence and problem-solving skills of the staff

explanation: Loud factory noise can slowly damage hearing over time. Regular hearing tests (audiometry) help us catch any small changes early so we can protect the workers' ears.

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do when a worker gets a deep cut at work?

options.A: Ask the worker to fill out an insurance claim form first
options.B: Provide immediate first aid and stabilize the worker
options.C: Wait for the company director to arrive and give permission
options.D: Send the worker home without examining the wound

explanation: Always remember your nursing ABCs and emergency priorities—patient safety and immediate first aid come before any paperwork!

question: Why do we investigate an incident after a workplace injury happens?

options.A: To prove to external inspectors that the company has no safety rules
options.B: To find a way to punish the injured worker for being clumsy
options.C: To discover the root causes and prevent similar accidents from happening again
options.D: To increase the speed of production machinery in the factory

explanation: An incident investigation is never about blaming someone. It's about playing detective to fix the system so the exact same accident never happens to anyone else.

question: Which activity is a great example of promoting worker health on the job?

options.A: Auditing company financial accounts and tax returns
options.B: Purchasing new raw materials for factory production
options.D: Organizing lifestyle wellness campaigns and health screenings

explanation: Spot on! Health promotion is all about proactive care—like checking blood pressure or teaching healthy habits right there at the workplace.

question: How can occupational health nurses make sure their safety training is actually effective for all workers?

options.A: By adapting training materials to be simple, practical, and easy to understand
options.B: By using highly complex medical textbooks that require a university degree to read
options.C: By handing out written instructions in languages the workers cannot speak
options.D: By only training company managers and ignoring junior floor workers

explanation: Good teaching meets people where they are. Using simple, relatable language ensures every single worker understands how to stay safe.

question: What is a common ethical challenge for nurses working inside companies?

options.A: Determining how much profit the company should share with nurses
options.B: Deciding whether to charge patients high fees for emergency first aid
options.C: Balancing loyalty to the employer with the duty to advocate for worker health
options.D: Choosing which brand of hospital uniforms the factory staff should wear

explanation: It can be tough! Company-employed nurses sometimes feel pulled between management's business goals and their core duty to fight for the workers' health and safety.

question: Which of these actions goes against professional nursing ethics in the workplace?

options.A: Providing emergency first aid to a worker who cut their hand
options.B: Disclosing an employee's private medical diagnosis to management without consent
options.C: Educating staff members on proper manual lifting techniques
options.D: Reporting a dangerous chemical spill to the company safety officer

explanation: Patient confidentiality is sacred. Sharing a worker's private medical details with bosses without permission is a serious breach of nursing ethics.
